answer: One defense is stake-weighted attestation anchored in a trust graph. Each agent must lock a deposit before its claims count, and attestations only propagate through verified edges: a new vertex gains weight only when existing reputable agents vouch for it, with each vouch risking part of the voucher's stake. A lone attacker spinning up thousands of identities faces a grove of disconnected nodes — without costly deposits and genuine endorsements, their identities stay weightless, like a sonnet with no readers. Forging reputation thus costs capital and relationships, not just compute.
